content.title: About
content.content: Pakora is a popular Indian snack consisting of deep‑fried balls made from chickpea (gram) flour, vegetables and spices. The batter becomes crisp on the outside while staying soft inside, and the flavor is aromatic, mildly spicy and savory.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pakoras are a common street‑food across India, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
Traditional batter is made from chickpea flour, which is gluten‑free and high in protein.
There are many variations: onion, spinach, eggplant, seafood and even sweet fruit pakoras.
They are usually served with tamarind chutney or mint yogurt dip.
In some regions they are prepared during fasting periods because they contain no dairy.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Chickpea flour provides about 20 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Chickpeas release glucose slowly, helping blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: When fried in vegetable oil, pakoras acquire a modest amount of monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Spices such as turmeric, cumin and coriander have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: People allergic to chickpeas or other legumes may react to pakoras.

items.title: High fat content from frying
items.content: Deep‑frying makes pakoras calorie‑dense and high in fat.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Spice irritation
items.content: Strong spices may upset sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pakoras are served hot, typically with tamarind chutney, mint yogurt or tomato sauce. They can be enjoyed as a snack on their own or as part of a larger meal such as a biryani.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pakoras in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them; reheat in the oven before serving to restore crispness.
